name: OSIRIS Intelligence Layer (payload-intel)
description: A small Express 5 service (intel/server.js, port 4000, container payload-intel) that acts as the ontology brain other Payload services query through GET /resolve: it ingests the OpenSanctions OFAC SDN CSV into an in-memory alias-normalised index refreshed every 24 h, queries Wikidata SPARQL and entity search on demand behind an LRU cache, and enriches IP addresses through ip-api.com and RIPE Stat, returning every answer as a typed {nodes, links} graph with SANCTIONS MATCH edges. Outbound requests are restricted to an allowlist of five domains, SPARQL inputs are sanitized, and each client IP is limited to 30 requests per minute. It holds no canonical state and writes nothing durable; the index is rebuilt at boot and a failed refresh keeps the stale copy. It must never become a person-profiling service: the person and abuse-contact paths it still serves sit in tension with the terminal's collection policy and are flagged for review.

capabilities.label: Service health
capabilities.description: GET /health returns status, sanctions_entries, sanctions_loaded_at, wikidata_cache_size and uptime_seconds; used by the container HEALTHCHECK every 30 s.
capabilities.provenance: this process: sanctions load time, Wikidata cache size and uptime

capabilities.label: Resolve an aircraft callsign
capabilities.description: GET /resolve?type=aircraft&id=<callsign>[&registration&model&icao24]: decodes the ICAO airline prefix via Wikidata (P230) into operator, HQ country, CEO and parent org; maps the registration prefix to a country; attaches the model; screens callsign, airline and registration against the OFAC SDN index. Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; id sanitized, 2-200 chars.
capabilities.provenance: Wikidata (P230 ICAO airline prefix), plus the OFAC SDN cross-reference

capabilities.label: Resolve a vessel by IMO or name
capabilities.description: GET /resolve?type=vessel&id=<imo|name>: Wikidata SPARQL by IMO number (P458) or English label under ship subclasses, yielding OWNED BY, OPERATED BY and FLAG STATE links, plus OFAC SDN cross-reference. Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; id sanitized, 2-200 chars.
capabilities.provenance: Wikidata SPARQL by IMO (P458) or ship-subclass label; OFAC SDN

capabilities.label: Resolve a company
capabilities.description: GET /resolve?type=company&id=<name>: Wikidata entity search to a QID then SPARQL for HEADQUARTERED country, PARENT ORG and CEO, plus OFAC SDN cross-reference of the company name. Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; id sanitized, 2-200 chars.
capabilities.provenance: Wikidata entity search and SPARQL; OFAC SDN

capabilities.label: Resolve a natural person (policy tension)
capabilities.description: GET /resolve?type=person&id=<name>: Wikidata search then SPARQL for NATIONALITY, EMPLOYER and POSITION HELD, plus OFAC SDN cross-reference. This path returns natural-person graphs, which the terminal's collection policy explicitly refuses on its own sanctions route; it is reachable through /api/entity/expand and should be reviewed.
capabilities.provenance: Wikidata search and SPARQL, and RIPE abuse contacts; OFAC SDN

capabilities.label: Resolve an IP address
capabilities.description: GET /resolve?type=ip&id=<address>: ip-api.com geolocation, ISP, org, ASN and proxy/hosting/mobile flags (HOSTED_BY, ASN, LOCATED_IN, GEOLOCATED links); RIPE Stat WHOIS netname, abuse contacts (returned as person nodes) and network-info prefix/ASNs; ISP and country screened against OFAC SDN. Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; id sanitized, 2-200 chars.
capabilities.provenance: ip-api.com geolocation, ISP, org and ASN

capabilities.label: Resolve a country
capabilities.description: GET /resolve?type=country&id=<name>: Wikidata head of state, capital, population, GDP, TLD, calling code, memberships (UN, NATO, EU...) and neighbours as typed nodes and links, plus OFAC SDN programme matches on the country name. Returns {nodes[{id,label,type,properties}], links[{source,target,label}], entity, source, sanctions_index_size, timestamp}; cached 24 h in an LRU of 10,000 keys; Cache-Control s-maxage=3600. Rate-limited 30/min per client IP; id sanitized, 2-200 chars.

capabilities.label: Ontology graph wire contract
capabilities.description: Every resolve response is a small typed graph: node types aircraft, vessel, company, person, ip, country, event, sanction; link labels such as OPERATED BY, OWNED BY, FLAG STATE, HEADQUARTERED, PARENT ORG, CEO, HOSTED_BY, ASN, SANCTIONS MATCH. Sanction nodes carry schema, countries, programs, aliases and sanctioned=true. The terminal renders it with react-force-graph-2d.
capabilities.provenance: whichever resolver answered; every node keeps the source that produced it

metadata.person_data_exception: Serves intel.resolve.person and returns RIPE abuse contacts as person nodes. It is the ontology service Payload Terminal calls, so the terminal's own CI gate against person routes is routed around by its dependency. Ends when /resolve drops the person and abuse-contact paths, or when the terminal stops forwarding type=person to it.

relations.description: Confirmed by code: the terminal's /api/entity/expand forwards type/id (and aircraft registration, model, icao24) to this service's GET /resolve at INTEL_URL and returns the ontology graph to the map's entity panel; docker-compose.yml runs both on the same network.

contracts.name: Resolve request
contracts.summary: GET /resolve?type=aircraft|vessel|company|person|ip|country&id=<2-200 chars>[&registration&model&icao24]; 400 on bad type/id, 429 on rate limit, 500 {error, nodes:[], links:[]} on failure.

contracts.name: Graph response
contracts.summary: {nodes, links, entity:{type,id}, source:"OSIRIS Intelligence Layer", sanctions_index_size, wikidata_cache_hits, timestamp}.

resources.name: OFAC SDN in-memory index
resources.description: Entries, aliases, countries, programs; refreshed every 24 h; stale copy kept on refresh failure.

resources.name: Wikidata LRU cache
resources.description: Up to 10,000 resolved graphs, 24 h TTL, per process.

external_services.name: Wikidata SPARQL and wbsearchentities
external_services.purpose: Entity ontology (operators, owners, flags, CEOs, countries)

reference.spatial: Carries coordinates only incidentally (ip-api city lat/lon on GEOLOCATED nodes; country nodes by name); no location of its own.
reference.temporal: sanctions_loaded_at and per-response timestamp; SDN first_seen per entry; no historical or as-of querying.
open_questions: Should the person resolver and the abuse-contact person nodes be removed to match the terminal's collection policy, or is the intel layer intentionally exempt?
ip-api.com is called over plain HTTP; is that acceptable for the deployment posture?
The service has no tests, no authentication and no outbound rate limiting toward Wikidata beyond caching; is it meant to stay a separate container or fold into the terminal?
The Wikidata User-Agent still names osirisai.live; should it carry the PayloadTerminal identity?

corpus.holding: An in-memory alias-normalised index of the OpenSanctions OFAC SDN list, refreshed every 24 hours, plus on-demand Wikidata and network enrichment behind an LRU cache.

COR-001.note: The index is one named list — the OFAC SDN CSV — plus on-demand lookups, and nothing durable.

COR-003.note: Answers are typed {nodes, links} graphs with SANCTIONS MATCH edges naming the list the match came from.

COR-004.note: sanctions_loaded_at and per-response timestamps exist, but there is no historical or as-of querying: what the index said last week cannot be recovered.

COR-005.note: A failed refresh silently keeps the stale copy rather than declaring staleness to the caller.

COR-006.note: There is no admission boundary. The SDN CSV is parsed straight into the index on fetch and trusted, and a failed refresh keeps the stale copy without declaring staleness — the same root as the COR-005 and COR-007 failures. Nothing validates what enters, so nothing can refuse it.

COR-007.note: The SDN CSV is parsed into memory on fetch; no capture is kept, so a revision upstream is unrecoverable.

COR-010.note: It must never become a person-profiling service, but the person and abuse-contact paths it still serves sit in tension with the terminal collection policy and remain unremoved.
